fieldMarks: Largest land mammal in North America; bulls about 900 kg, cows about 500 kg
Dark chocolate-brown with long hair on the head, shoulders and forelegs and short hair on the flanks and hindquarters
Both sexes carry short, upward-curving horns
Calves are reddish-tan at birth and begin turning brown after about 2.5 months
behavior: Herds of cows and young appear to be led by older females; groups average about 20 in winter and about 200 in summer
Rut in July and August: bulls bellow, wallow and fight
Grazes grasses and sedges 9–11 hours a day; swings its head to clear snow
Rubs on trees and rocks and uses dirt wallows
habitat: Open plains and grasslands in the south; boreal forest openings, meadows and river valleys in the north; attracted to recently burned areas.
range: Once widespread from Alaska and western Canada across the U.S. into northern Mexico; now in isolated herds within and outside the historical range. Yellowstone is the only place in the lower 48 states with a continuously free-ranging population since prehistoric times.
